Subject: Private deployment intake — initial constraints and questions

Marissa,

Thanks again for taking our call this morning. As promised, a short note with the immediate constraints and the ask from ClearGrove IT so we can scope the on‑prem deployment properly. High level: we need a private Redwood control plane inside our VPC with on‑prem inference nodes in our datacenter. Key constraints: 

- Network: egress to Redwood-hosted control plane only allowed over an approved peering connection; no open inbound from internet to nodes.
- Data residency: model cache and KV must live on local NVMe; logs forwarded to our SIEM over TLS only.
- Hardware: 2 racks initially — we expect 8x A100-equivalent GPUs across 6 nodes.
- Storage: combination of fast NVMe for cache (ephemeral + replicate) and a network blockstore for model artifacts/backups.

Open questions for you/your team that will affect sizing and the contract: 
1) Does Redwood support an air-gapped or restricted‑egress control plane model (we prefer peering + mutual TLS)?
2) Recommended nodepool split for production vs. canary traffic and preemptible burst?
3) Persistent volume recommendations for model artifacts vs ephemeral KV caches (encryption + snapshot cadence)?
4) Any preflight checklist we should run prior to site visit?

We can host an on‑site workshop the week of Feb 23 — ideally bring a solutions engineer and someone from infra to map the network and run a live preflight. Please loop in whoever owns the private deploy plan at Redwood.

Thanks,
Daniel Ruiz
Director, Infrastructure — ClearGrove Health
ops-eng@cleargrove.com

Daniel — appreciate the clear list. Looping in Karthik (solutions), Laura (customer success) and Irene (field ops) so we can produce a compact plan and preflight. Quick answers inline, then proposed next steps.

1) Control plane & network: We support a private control plane with VPC peering and mTLS for control traffic. Air‑gapped deployments are possible but require an on‑prem control plane package (longer lead time). We will document the peering ACLs and ports.

2) Nodepool split: recommendation below from Karthik but short version — 3 nodepools: 
   - prod (baseline, non-preemptible) — 4 nodes, GPU velocity for steady traffic
   - canary (small footprint) — 1–2 smaller GPU nodes for validation
   - burst (preemptible/burst) — 2 nodes for batch and peak loads

3) Storage: short answer — NVMe local for KV/cache + encrypted NBD for model artifacts with regular snapshots to your backup service. We'll include snapshot cadence options (hourly vs 6hr) in the preflight.

4) Preflight: attaching a Redwood preflight checklist (redwood-preflight-checklist.pdf). Please complete items A1–A6 and share the network team contact.

Proposed next steps:
- Karthik will draft a site runbook (node profiles, IO budget, expected token throughput).
- Laura will prepare the onboarding milestones and contract checklist (SLA, data handling).
- Irene will coordinate an on‑site or remote workshop week of Feb 23.

Are you able to share utilization targets (rps, avg sequence len) and preferred maintenance windows? If you can populate the nodepool-sizing.xlsx I attached, Karthik can precompute PV provisioning guidance.

Marissa

Daniel / team — thanks for the details. I sketched a technical checklist and a recommended baseline which I’ve pasted below. I’ll bring a detailed runbook to the workshop.

Summary recommendations (baseline production footprint):
- Control plane: VPC peered control-plane + control-plane proxy in your VPC. mTLS on port 8443, outbound to 34.98.12.45 (Redwood control) via static NAT.
- Cluster: k8s 1.26+, 3 master-like controlplane nodes (co-located or separate from inference nodes depending on air-gapped needs).
- Nodepools & sizing:
  * nodepool-prod: 4 x 4‑GPU nodes (A100 equivalent), 256GB RAM each, local NVMe 7TB per node for KV/cache (encrypted).
  * nodepool-canary: 1 x 1‑GPU node, 128GB RAM, local NVMe 1TB.
  * nodepool-burst: 1–2 x 2‑GPU preemptible nodes, smaller NVMe but larger ephemeral CPU / network egress budget.
- Storage:
  * Model artifacts: network blockstore (iSCSI/CSI) with encryption at rest, daily snapshot to backup target.
  * KV/Prefix cache: local NVMe with periodic replication to sibling node (async) to speed warm starts. Ephemeral by default; durable copy on artifact updates.
- Networking / Egress: All nodes must allow outbound 443/8443 to control-plane IPs only. No inbound NAT from internet to inference nodes. BGP peering optional for large customers.
- Observability: Forward logs to your SIEM (TLS) and push Prometheus remote_write to our secure relay if you want Redwood visibility.
- Failure domains: spread prod nodes across two racks + separate PD for NVMe. Plan for one‑rack failure.

Preflight items we need you to confirm before site visit (short):
A1) VLAN ranges for nodes and control-plane proxies
A2) NAT/static IPs we should whitelist (control-plane egress)
A3) NVMe vendor/firmware version (for encryption toolchain)
A4) Backup target (S3-compatible endpoint) and snapshot retention policy
A5) Maintenance window preferences (UTC offset)
A6) Test dataset for load profile (token size distribution)

I’ll attach a short shell checklist and sample kube manifests in the workshop folder. If you can populate the nodepool-sizing.xlsx with expected rps and median sequence length, I’ll produce PV sizing and IO ops/sec budgets.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
